absent: Numeric values and definitions of base and end addresses, entry size, entry limits and page protections.
Allocation, slot address computation, locked table lookup, remote flush, entry fill and emptiness test helpers.
Full layouts of address space context, descriptor table, hardware and user descriptors beyond observed fields.
Paravirtual allocation hooks and sanity check worker behavior.
Trampoline contents, control code size limit, handoff index values and processor state save details.
Sixty four bit transfer, debug table setup completion, prepare and cleanup bodies beyond the cut fragment.
Error code numeric values and user copy semantics beyond observed return paths.

findings.text: Address space lifecycle can duplicate local descriptor state into a child, destroy the installed table, and release the reserved paging range on unmap exit.
User space reaches descriptor management through one system entry that selects among read, legacy write, default read and modern write behaviors.
Thirty two bit staged reboot exposes a prepare step that makes control code executable and builds tables, a cleanup step that reverses them, and a transfer step that jumps to the staged image.
Sixty four bit file loading publishes a null terminated loader table whose only entry supports the sixty four bit compressed image format.
Modify descriptor system entry dispatches on its first selector and falls back to not implemented for unknown values before narrowing the result.

Thirty two bit transfer entry accepts a staged image descriptor, copies trampoline code into its control page, programs a handoff array, reloads segments, invalidates tables and invokes the trampoline.
Publication and duplication serialize on the per address space context mutex, with publication using release ordering followed by a synchronous refresh on all processors sharing the address space.
User visible reads hold the descriptor user semaphore shared while writes hold it exclusively with killable wait, so readers overlap but writers exclude each other and readers.
Each leaf install or clear is performed under the owning page table spin protection with unmap followed by a range flush in the same address space.
Reclaim of the reserved descriptor interval uses a full address space gather object around a range free to avoid incremental range tracking.
A small walk carrier pairs a mapping configuration pointer with a top level table pointer and is passed as opaque context to the resource callback.
Observed descriptor state carries an entry array pointer, an entry count, and a slot marker where a negative value means not yet mapped.
Thirty two bit staged image stores a top table pointer plus two leaf pages and, under extended paging, two middle pages.
Sixty four bit staged image stores four single pages forming one branch of the transition walk.
Thirty two bit handoff uses a flat array with dedicated positions for control physical address, control virtual address, top table physical address and optional swap page.
Descriptor write allocates a successor, copies predecessor bytes, stores the new entry, finalizes, maps the alternate slot, publishes, then unmaps and frees the predecessor.

Duplication does nothing when there is no source or no installed table, otherwise it locks the source, allocates an equal sized table, copies bytes, finalizes, maps at slot zero and on failure reclaims and frees before unlocking.

Thirty two bit execution saves processor and tracing state, disables interrupts and breakpoints, optionally restores legacy interrupt mode, copies trampoline, reloads segments, invalidates descriptor caches, jumps, then restores saved state on return.

Sixty four bit table build allocates a top page, maps recorded physical ranges, then maps image segments, firmware system table, firmware tables and debug serial, finishing with the transition alias which must be last.
Transition branch creation descends levels allocating any missing zeroed intermediate page and linking it with kernel table protections before installing the final executable leaf.

Descriptor user mapping work is active only when the boot processor reports the isolation feature, otherwise mapping reports success trivially, unmapping does nothing and range reclaim returns immediately.
Each descriptor object is expected to be mapped at most once and current mappings are sanity checked by observing presence in kernel and user top entries.
Isolated descriptor pages are installed read only without the global hint with unsupported protection bits masked out, with page count derived by rounding entry bytes up.
Propagation to the user top table happens only when isolation is active and the address space currently has no descriptor table installed.
Successor size is the larger of predecessor size and requested index plus one, so writes never shrink the table.
Reads clamp the request to an architectural maximum, copy at most the installed bytes, zero fill any shortfall and report the clamped request length.
Default table reads return zeroed bytes up to an architecture dependent ceiling, larger on thirty two bit than the fixed small sixty four bit value.
Sixteen bit entries need build support and are refused under paravirtual Xen guests with a one time notice, otherwise they are allowed.

Writes require exact control structure size and in range index, reject a risky type encoding unless the segment is marked absent under the modern operation mode, and treat zero base with zero limit or an empty descriptor as a clear.
Unmapping clears each installed leaf across the rounded page count and then flushes the corresponding virtual interval.
Destruction frees the context table and clears the pointer while unmap exit only reclaims the reserved paging range.
Thirty two bit table allocation obtains zeroed pages for required levels and reports out of memory if any is missing, while freeing releases each level and clears the stored pointer.
Single mapping helper links missing upper levels to supplied lower pages with present style protections then installs an executable kernel leaf for the supplied frame.
Thirty two bit preparation maps the control page at its kernel virtual address with one leaf page and identity at its physical address with the other leaf page, choosing middle pages by paging mode.
Firmware table mapping walks two resource kinds and treats absent descriptor as success while propagating other failures, with a null variant that always succeeds.
Debug serial mapping is skipped when no address is configured, otherwise a page aligned window covering the device plus small slack is mapped with an informational message.

Firmware system table mapping is skipped when boot services are absent or the address is zero, otherwise it maps the header then remaps the configuration array sized by table count, with width selected by firmware bitness.
Transition setup ensures the control page is reachable at the kernel virtual alias derived from its physical location in addition to identity coverage.
When guest memory encryption is active the transition leaf and bulk mapping flags include encryption, otherwise the transition uses a no encryption executable protection.
Bulk construction page allocator requests single control pages from the staged image, clears them on success and returns null on exhaustion.

Thirty two bit segment reload performs a far jump to the kernel code selector then loads data selectors into data and stack registers, while sixty four bit reload loads the kernel data selector into data and segment base registers without a jump.
Swap page address is published only for the default image type, and preserving jumps save processor state, clear and restore interrupt mode, then restore processor state on return.
Mapping failure during first installation can leave a partially populated leaf page that the caller must mop up, while installation over an existing table is expected not to fail that way.
Write waits killably and reports interruption, user copy faults report fault, and malformed requests report invalid argument without changing installed state.
Freeing chooses virtual release versus single page release by whether entry bytes exceed one page, so mismatched allocation sizing would corrupt memory.
After forcing segment state the transfer invalidates global and interrupt descriptor caches, so further descriptor loads need caller supplied tables and interrupts must stay disabled.
Operation selectors zero, one, two and seventeen hexadecimal select read, legacy write, default read and modern write respectively.
System result is narrowed to thirty two bits on return so negative codes occupy only the low half of the result register without extension into the high half.
Reclaim operates over the interval delimited by the isolated descriptor base and end markers.
Sixty four bit reboot logging prefixes messages with a short subsystem tag.
